Title: Positive expression of miR-361-5p indicates better prognosis for breast cancer patients.
Source: Journal of thoracic disease (2016)
Abstract: BACKGROUND: MicroRNA-361-5p (miR-361-5p) has been reported to be tumor suppressor in colorectal, gastric and prostate cancer, but as an oncogene in cervical cancer. key_findings.finding: In a breast-cancer tissue microarray study of 375 patients, positive tumor-tissue miR-361-5p staining (295/375, 78.7%) was associated with better disease-free survival: median DFS 95.52 vs 82.33 months for negative staining (P=0.002); the association was strongest in triple-negative breast cancer (P=0.004). The authors described miR-361-5p as an independent predictive factor, although the accessible abstract does not provide the multivariable covariates, hazard ratio, or confidence interval. This is direct human tumor-tissue evidence favoring better prognosis. [PMID 27499968]

source_tools.relevance: Direct clinical breast-cancer tissue study with DFS, TNBC subgroup, and independence claim

key_findings.finding: A separate TCGA breast-tumor analysis found that higher miR-361-5p expression was positively correlated with improved breast-cancer survival; miR-361-5p was among the 12 mature miRNAs associated with improved survival and was selected for further analysis. This supports a favorable direction for overall survival, but the accessible report does not show a breast-cancer-specific hazard ratio, confidence interval, or a conventional multivariable Cox model, so the strength and independence of the OS association cannot be fully verified from the retrieved text.

source_tools.relevance: Direct TCGA human breast-tumor survival analysis

key_findings.finding: Evidence is not completely uniform: a 2021 TCGA-based breast-tissue study focused on miRNA reference-gene stability reported that miR-361-5p had no significant association with overall survival in its analysis, while acknowledging the prior positive DFS finding specifically in TNBC. Thus, the favorable association is replicated directionally in some datasets but not consistently for OS.

source_tools.relevance: Explicitly reports no significant OS association and contrasts it with prior TNBC DFS evidence

key_findings.finding: The retrieved breast-cancer clinical evidence concerns tumor tissue/TCGA tumor expression, not circulating miR-361-5p in serum, plasma, or exosomes. The targeted circulating-expression search did not identify a direct human breast-cancer prognostic study for circulating miR-361-5p; therefore no conclusion about circulating miR-361-5p and survival, relapse, metastasis, or stage is supported here.

source_tools.relevance: Targeted serum/plasma/circulating breast-cancer search; returned no direct prognostic breast-cancer study among the relevant results

key_findings.finding: For tumor stage, lymph-node/distant metastasis, and relapse specifically, the retrieved direct breast-cancer reports do not provide a clear clinical association for miR-361-5p. The 2016 tissue study reports DFS but its accessible abstract does not report stage/metastasis distributions or relapse-specific effect estimates; the TCGA report addresses survival rather than stage or metastasis. Other retrieved miR-361-5p results were about non-breast cancers or mechanistic studies and should not be used as breast-cancer prognosis evidence.
